units.title: Whole Numbers
units.intro: In this unit you make **number patterns**, find formulas for **even** and **odd** numbers, learn the **order of operations**, and use the **properties** of whole numbers.

cards.title: Three kinds of numbers
body: **Natural numbers** begin with 1: $1, 2, 3, 4, \ldots$
**Whole numbers** are 0 and the counting numbers: $\{0, 1, 2, 3, \ldots\}$
**Integers** are the whole numbers and the negatives of the natural numbers.

cards.title: Natural numbers on a number line
body: Natural numbers start at 1 and go on for ever.

cards.title: Even and odd dot patterns
body: Niema uses **pairs** of dots: $2, 4, 6, 8$ are **even**.
Elsa's patterns always have **one dot left over**: $1, 3, 5, 7$ are **odd**.

cards.q: Which of these numbers is odd? $38, 47, 96$
cards.why: $47$ ends in 7. It cannot be split into pairs (p. 3).

cards.title: Formula for the V-pattern
body: Zahra's formula: the $n$th V-pattern has $2n + 1$ dots.

cards.title: Which V-pattern?

cards.title: Even and odd formulas
body: **Odd** numbers: $2n - 1$ (Alem).
**Even** numbers: $2n$ (Adem).
Here $n$ is a natural number.

cards.problem: Find the 12th even number and the 12th odd number.

cards.title: Find n

cards.title: Even or odd?
body: Look at the last digit: $0, 2, 4, 6, 8$ → even.

cards.title: Rule 2
body: With addition or subtraction **and** multiplication, do the **multiplication first**.

steps.text: Work from left to right: divide first.

cards.title: Rule 3
body: With **multiplication and division**, work **from left to right**.

cards.title: Rule 4
body: With **brackets**, do the operation in the brackets **first**.

cards.title: Order of operations
body: **B**rackets, then **×÷**, then **+−**.

body: $3 \times 5 = 15$ and $5 \times 3 = 15$.

cards.title: Commutative property
body: For any whole numbers $a$ and $b$:
$a + b = b + a$ (addition)
$a \times b = b \times a$ (multiplication)

cards.title: Associative property
body: $(a \times b) \times c = a \times (b \times c)$

cards.title: Distributive property
body: $a \times (b + c) = (a \times b) + (a \times c)$
$a \times (b - c) = (a \times b) - (a \times c)$

body: **C**hange order, **A**rrange brackets, **D**istribute.

units.title: Rational Numbers
units.intro: In this unit you meet **fractions** and **rational numbers**. You change mixed fractions, find **equivalent fractions**, and **add, subtract, multiply and divide** fractions.

loaf.title: A loaf cut into 8 equal parts

addpie.title: Azmara and Zahra shade a circle

steps.text: Weizero Zeineb cut one loaf into **8 equal parts**.
Yosuf got 3 parts: $\frac{3}{8}$ of the loaf.

cards.title: Numerator and denominator
body: In $\frac{3}{8}$, **3** is the **numerator** (top).
**8** is the **denominator** (bottom). It tells how many equal parts.

cards.title: Sharing cakes
cards.problem: Two cakes are shared equally by 5 children. What is each child's share?

cards.title: Rational numbers
body: A number that can be written as $\frac{a}{b}$ with $b \neq 0$ is a **rational number**.

cards.q: In a group of 10 students, 6 are boys. What fraction are girls?

cards.title: Equivalent fractions
body: $\frac{2}{5}, \frac{4}{10}, \frac{6}{15}, \frac{8}{20}$ are **equivalent fractions**.
Multiply or divide the numerator **and** the denominator by the **same number**.

cards.title: Are they equivalent?
cards.problem: Are $\frac{5}{7}$ and $\frac{15}{21}$ equivalent?

cards.title: Proper, improper, mixed
body: **P**roper is **P**etite on top. **I**mproper is **I**nflated.

cards.title: Rule for the same denominator
body: $\frac{a}{c} + \frac{b}{c} = \frac{a + b}{c}$
$\frac{a}{c} - \frac{b}{c} = \frac{a - b}{c}$

cards.problem: Find $\frac{3}{4} + \frac{2}{5}$.

steps.text: Make twentieths: multiply $\frac{3}{4}$ by $\frac{5}{5}$ and $\frac{2}{5}$ by $\frac{4}{4}$.

steps.text: Add the wholes and the parts separately.

steps.text: Group the wholes and the fractions.

cards.title: Which is greater: 3/4 or 5/8?
body: The number further right is greater.

body: **S**ame, **A**dd, then tidy up **M**ixed numbers.

body: Three daughters each give $\frac{1}{4}$ of an orange to their brother.

cards.title: The brother's share
cards.problem: What part of the oranges did the brother receive?

cards.title: Multiplying fractions
body: $\frac{a}{b} \times \frac{c}{d} = \frac{a \times c}{b \times d}$
Example: $\frac{2}{3} \times \frac{4}{5} = \frac{8}{15}$.

cards.title: Simplify first
cards.problem: Find $\frac{3}{4} \times \frac{2}{9}$.

cards.title: Reciprocals
body: If the product of two numbers is **1**, they are **reciprocals**.
$\frac{a}{b}$ and $\frac{b}{a}$ are reciprocals ($a, b \neq 0$).
$0$ is the only number with **no** reciprocal.

cards.title: Dividing fractions
body: Dividing by a number is the same as **multiplying by its reciprocal**.
$\frac{a}{b} \div \frac{c}{d} = \frac{a}{b} \times \frac{d}{c}$

cards.title: Divide by a fraction
cards.problem: Find $\frac{9}{16} \div \frac{3}{4}$.

steps.text: Flip the second fraction and multiply.

units.title: Finding the Unknowns
units.intro: In this unit you use **letters** like $x$ for unknown numbers. You write **expressions** and **equations**, find their values, and **simplify** by grouping similar terms.

cards.title: Using a letter
body: Araia is **4 years older** than Ali.
When Ali is $x$ years old, Araia is $x + 4$ years old.
Here $x$ stands for a whole number.

cards.q: Ali is 9 now. How old will he be in $x$ years?

units.title: Graphs
units.intro: In this unit you use **two variables** $x$ and $y$, write **ordered pairs**, and **plot points** and **straight-line graphs** on the number plane.

cards.title: Two variables

Araia is 4 years older, so $y = x + 4$.

body: A pair like $(1, 5)$ is an **ordered pair**.
The first number is $x$, the second is $y$.

cards.title: Number plane
body: Two number lines drawn **perpendicular** to each other form a **number plane**.
The point where the axes cross is the **origin**.

steps.text: Right of the origin: $x$ is positive. Left: negative.

units.title: Lines and Angles
units.intro: In this unit you tell apart **lines**, **line segments** and **rays**. You name **angles** by their size, and meet **adjacent**, **complementary** and **supplementary** angles.

cards.title: The skipping rope
body: The girls' hands hold the rope at two points.
Those points show the **ends** of a **line segment**.
A pencil, a ruler and a stick are all examples of line segments.

cards.title: Line segment
body: A **line segment** $AB$ is the set of points $A$, $B$ and all points between them.

steps.text: A **line segment** has two end points.
A **ray** has one end point and goes on in one direction.

cards.q: Which has exactly two end points?
cards.why: A line segment has two end points (p. 60).

cards.title: Count the ends
body: **L**ine, **R**ay, **S**egment: $0, 1, 2$ ends.

cards.title: Angle BAC
body: Two rays with the **same end point** form an **angle**.
The end point is the **vertex**.

cards.title: Naming an angle
body: This is angle $BAC$, written $\angle BAC$.
The vertex letter $A$ goes in the **middle**.

cards.title: A cute little angle
body: An **acute** angle is **a cute** little angle.

cards.title: More than two rays
body: Several rays can share one end point $O$.
They make many angles, such as $\angle BOC$, $\angle COD$ and $\angle AOF$.

cards.title: Name some angles
cards.problem: Name three angles in the figure that have $OC$ as a side.

steps.text: Start at C, go to O, then to another point.
The vertex $O$ is always in the middle.

cards.title: Remember
body: When naming angles at a point, the shared end point $O$ is always the middle letter.

steps.text: They have no interior point in common: they are **adjacent**.

cards.title: Complementary angles
body: Two angles whose measures add up to $90^\circ$ are **complementary**.

cards.title: 60° and 30°

$60^\circ + 30^\circ = 90^\circ$.

units.title: Triangles and Quadrilaterals
units.intro: In this unit you sort **triangles** by their **sides** and **angles**, use the **angle sum** of a triangle ($180^\circ$), and meet the family of **quadrilaterals**.

cards.title: Triangle
body: Using three rays we can make a **three-sided figure**. It is called a **triangle**.
Triangles are classified by their **sides** and by their **angles** (p. 71).

cards.title: Legs and base
body: The two congruent sides of an isosceles triangle are the **legs**.
The third side is the **base**.

cards.title: Is equilateral also isosceles?
body: All equilateral triangles are isosceles triangles.
But not all isosceles triangles are equilateral: the three sides may not be congruent.

cards.title: Angle sum
body: The angles of a triangle add up to $180^\circ$.

cards.title: Equiangular triangle
cards.problem: An equiangular triangle has three congruent angles. Find each angle.

cards.title: Base angles
body: In an isosceles triangle, $\angle C$ is the **vertex angle**. $\angle A$ and $\angle B$ are the **base angles**.
If two base angles are equal, the triangle is isosceles.

cards.title: Right angled triangle
body: A right angled triangle has **one right angle**.
The side opposite the right angle is the **hypotenuse**.

steps.text: Roble, Senait and Mihret use straws of 6 cm, 8 cm and 10 cm.
The legs are 6 and 8. The hypotenuse is 10.

cards.title: Obtuse and acute triangles
body: An **obtuse triangle** has one obtuse angle. The other two add up to less than $90^\circ$.
An **acute triangle** has three acute angles.

steps.text: In $\triangle PQR$ the angles are $73^\circ$, $58^\circ$ and $49^\circ$.
The side opposite it, $QR$, is the longest side.

cards.title: Equilateral with x

cards.title: Median
body: Arrange the data in order and take the **middle** score.
With an even number of items, the median is the **average of the two middle scores**.

cards.title: Mode
body: The **mode** is the score that occurs **most often**.
There can be more than one mode. If every number occurs equally often, there is no mode.
